questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

My parents have booked a mini-getaway for me.

options.text: A mini-getaway was being booked for me by my parents.
A mini-getaway had been booked for me by my parents.
A mini-getaway was been booked for me by my parents.
A mini-getaway has been booked for me by my parents.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e. 'A mini-getaway has been booked for me by my parents.'

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **active voice.** We have to change the sentence into **passive form. **
 
• The given sentence is written in **'present perfect tense.'**
 
• The structure of these kinds of sentences is:
 
 
• **Active Voice:** Subject + has/have + V3 + Object.
 
• **Passive Voice: **Object + has/have + been + V3 + by (preposition) + Subject.
 
 
 
• Let’s see another example:
 
 
• **Active voice:** The police have opened a file on the case.
 
• **Passive voice: **A file has been opened by the police on the case.
 
 
 
• The subject of the given sentence is** 'My parents' **and the object of the given sentence is** 'a mini-getaway'. **
 
• So, in the passive voice, the position of ‘subject’ and ‘object’ will be interchanged. 
 
• Also here,** 'have booked'** will be changed into **'has been booked'.**

 

**Correct Sentence:**__* A mini-getaway has been booked for me by my parents.*

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

There is some monkeys / on the roof of the / carriage but Madhav / does not see them.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is option 2) i.e. 'There is some monkeys.' 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ​The word "some" is typically used with uncountable nouns or **plural nouns** when referring to an indefinite quantity.
 
• However, when referring to a specific number of monkeys on the roof, it would be more appropriate to use **"there are"** instead of "there is."
 
• **"Is"** is used with** singular nouns**, while "are" is used with **plural nouns**.
 
• In this case, since we are talking about multiple monkeys (a plural noun), the correct verb form should be **"are."**
 
• By using "are" instead of "is," we maintain grammatical agreement between the plural noun "monkeys" and the verb "are."
 
• Also, the pronoun "them" (in the latter part of the sentence) is used to refer to the monkeys. "Them" is a** plural pronoun**, indicating that there are multiple monkeys.

Therefore, the correct answer is: *There **are** some monkeys on the roof of the carriage, but Madhav does not see them*.

__
